steps.text: In a large pan over low heat, cook butter, sugar and water until butter is melted. Add chocolate chips and stir until partially melted. Remove from heat and continue to stir until chocolate is completely melted. Pour into a large bowl and let stand 10 minutes to cool off slightly.
At high speed, beat in eggs, one at a time into chocolate mixture. Reduce speed to low and add dry ingredients, beating until blended. Chill dough about 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Roll dough into balls and place on ungreased cookie sheet about 2 inches apart. Bake 8-10 minutes. While cookies are baking unwrap mints and divide each in half. When cookies are brought out of the oven, put 1/2 mint on top of each cookie. Let the mint sit for up to 5 minutes until melted, then spread the mint on top of the cookie. Eat and enjoy!

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Mint Cookies I
raw_recipe.description: This is a melt in your mouth chocolate cookie that has a chocolate mint frosting. It's delicious and it's easy!

review.reviewBody: Wonderful recipe! The only thing I did different was, I found Andes baking pieces in the store so I mixed 2 cups of them up with the dough and skipped the "frosting" portion. They are so yummy...I plan to give them as Christmas gifts.

What a fabulous cookie! Using the microwave made this so much easier! I put the butter, brown sugar and water in the microwave for 1 minute, stirred until the butter was melted, then added the chocolate (see below) and cooked another minute. I made do with what I had on hand, so I used 1 cup of semisweet chocolate chips and 1 cup of the Andes baking pieces. It made the dough nice and minty! When they were done baking, I put about a measuring teaspoon of the Andes baking bits on top for a few minutes before spreading them to make the frosting. I know some of you used the Andes bits in the cookie and not as a frosting, but to me the frosting makes it a 5-star recipe! I plan to use the green Andes mints at Christmas for the top and take these along to our cookie exchange. Highly recommended!

Superb recipe - great tasting and easy to make! I go all out and put a full Andes mint on top of each cookie. The chocolate melts down into all the cookie crevices creating perfect cookie goodness! For those who said the cookies were flat, the butter probably wasn't cold enough. Before rolling into balls, put the dough in the fridge for 15-30 minutes. The chilled dough allows it not to spread so quickly in the oven, resulting in a thicker cookie. Also, use a cookie scoop to ensure all the cookies are the same size and cook evenly for the same amount of time. These cookies are pretty but they taste even better. Perfect for a cookie exchange and just as good 2-3 days later as the first day (and I'm not really a chocolate cookie person!!!).

Just the right amount of chewy... Very easy to make and taste very good! I think melting the butter and sugar over the stove top makes all the difference. I did stray away from the recipe a little bit, I subbed the mint candies for marshmallows and they were heavenly! So instead of the candies, I took the cookies out about 2 minutes before they were done and added half of a large marshmallow onto each cookie, then broiled it for a minute to toast the marshmallows.

This is my "famous" holiday cookie recipe. I crush candycanes by putting them in a bag (and put another bag over it, in case the bag punctures) and wacking them with a hammer. I put about a tsp of the fine dust into the batter and then decorate by putting the candycane bits on top of the "frosting". It is a HUGE hit at the office every year. A co-worker loves them so much that he has been known to eat NINE in one 3 hour period. I am not allowed to make anything else during the December pot-luck. :)

Just wonderful, melt in your mouth cookies. Chilled the dough for more than an hour, and had no issues with sticky dough. Scooped them out with a small cookie/meatball scoop which made rolling them a breeze. Baked them for 8 minutes, and left them on the cookie sheet for 5 minutes while the Andes mints were melting. Found it helpful to have the mints cut and ready to go, so they can be put on the cookie right away, allowing them to melt beautifully. I swirled the melted mint wafer with the think side of a flat toothpick. This prevented loss of chocolate on a bigger utensil and allowed the two colors of the wafer to shine more. They were the hit of my kiddo's school bake sale! Thanks for a great recipe.

These cookies are so yummy! I used a level scoop that held 1 1/2 tbsp to size each cookie and got 43 cookies. Baked them for about 9 1/2 minutes at 350. They are very delicate when warm so I let them stay on the cookie sheet for a couple of minutes before transferring to a cooling surface. That 2 minutes is a perfect time to put one Andes mint on each cookie. Smear the melted mint a couple of minutes after removing from the cookie sheet.

I have made these several times at Christmas-but this year made a couple changes. I didn't think it would be possible to improve on such a good recipe but I think I actually did!! I added 1 tsp Peppermint extract to the dough, followed another reviewers suggestion to only stir flour with a wooden spoon-great suggestion! I also used the dark chocolate mint (dark with green in the middle) Hershey Kisses! These are amazing, soft and perfect when following the baking directions exactly as in the recipe.

Delicious! Like a thin mint only way better! At first I tried to cheat and MIX chopped Andes in with the batter, but once I finished the cookies they weren't minty enough so I put the candy on the top to melt. WOW, so good with them mixed in and melted on top! One thing I would do different is shape into balls BEFORE I chill the dough because once the dough was chilled I had a heck of a time scooping it (in fairness I chilled it all night). I had to let it sit out awhile. My cookies came out a bit flat, but they were super good so I won't try to fix that. I took them out of the oven when they still looked raw, and they cooled nice and chewy. Really good cookies!

I made this recipe as written but baked them a little differently. I baked the cookies 9 mins. Then I took them out added the half mint. Put back in oven for another 1 or 2 mins. Took them out swirled the mint with a toothpick to make a little chocolate puddle then sprinkled crush candy canes on the melted chocolate puddle. Even my hubby commented how good these cookies are. Ive had this type cookie before but not this recipe. This is a keeper for any Christmas cookie tray. Perfect!!!!

These cookies were fantastic. Chocolate cookies don't usually temp me, but I couldn't stay away from these. I added 3/4 teaspoon espresso powder to the butter/chocolate mixture to enhance the chocolate flavor. Also, I made some of the cookies with the Andes mints and some with Hershey's tuxedo kisses. I didn't spread the kisses, but rather left them in their kiss form. The white kiss was a nice visual contrast to the chocolate and the flavor was delicious! I'm making more of each variety for New Year's Eve party favors. I'll add stickers to my treat bags that say, "Kiss 2017 bye-bye" and "2018 is 'mint' to be fabulous".
Makes a lot of cookies. Turns out good using cup 4 cup flour as I have a gluten allergy.
This is a great cookie recipe! My friends and family request these cookies all the time. The only change I made to this recipe is, I use peppermint patties on top.
No changes made. Loved as is!
Tremendous! I went crazy and used ghirardelli mint chocolate squares. They were deadly.
My aunt makes these every year and they’re my favorite! Once the Andes is melted, she uses a spatula to spread the frosting and adds sprinkles. Mmmmm

Absolutely wonderful cookies! I get asked for the recipe every year and my grandson is obsessed with them. This year I bought the Andes mints in advance because they are hard to find around the holidays.
